## Before you start the log {.center}

### What you are about to measure

A temperature sensor, in an insulated box, logged for **24 hours**.

Nothing you would call "the temperature" is supposed to change much. What
you are actually measuring is:

- how much the *instrument itself* wanders, with no help from the room;
- how much the room gets through the insulation anyway, on a cycle you
  already know the period of;
- and — the headline result — **how long you should average for**, and what
  happens if you average for longer than that.

### The rule of the session

::: {.callout-important}
## More averaging is not always better

Every earlier experiment on this site showed noise falling as you average
more. This one finds the point where that stops being true — and shows what
takes over once it does.
:::

## At the bench {.center}

### What you will build

An insulated enclosure — a cooler box, foam, whatever slows heat exchange
with the room — with the sensor near its centre, away from the walls.

::: {.callout-warning}
## This one runs overnight

Disable host sleep and unattended updates before you start. Label the setup
with what it is and when it should finish. See the handbook's safety
callout before you leave it.
:::

### One long recording

```bash
arduino-io mode 15 analog
arduino-io stream 15 --hz 0.2 --seconds 86400 --csv data/log-24h.csv
```

Watch the first few records land before you walk away. Come back in at least
24 hours, stop the stream, and check the record for gaps before trusting it.

### Then

Open [the handbook](handbook.qmd) for the full procedure, and one of the two
analysis templates — [Python](analysis-py.qmd) or [R](analysis-r.qmd).

They have the same sections and produce the same numbers. Both ship with a
24-hour reference log, so you can read the whole analysis before your own run
finishes.

## What you should come away with {.center}

### Three sentences you should be able to defend

1. "This record's drift is $\dot x$ mK/h, and the diurnal cycle — $A_d$ mK,
   the largest single feature in the raw data — is the room, not the
   instrument."
2. "The Allan deviation of the detrended residual has a minimum at
   $\tau_\mathrm{opt} = \dots$, of $\sigma_y = \dots$; averaging past that
   point makes the answer *worse*, not better."
3. "The correct Type A term for a 24-hour average of this record is
   $\sigma_y(\tau_\mathrm{opt})$, not $s/\sqrt n$, because the record is not
   made of independent samples."

If you can say those three with your own numbers in them, the session
worked.
